set.request: I feel like we need some alternate UI themes. how do we create a better theme browser for all these things? maybe column based pages can allow us to organize trees of themes? can we algorithmically create themes?
set.now: verified at 400 / 1280 / 3440 and in dark mode; no console errors
steps: Ground truth: color study, lew42.css, theme guide, columns convention
Name and build 5 alternate themes as token-override CSS
Build the mock mini-UI, painted once per theme
Build the OKLCH generator (seed -> tokens, contrast by construction)
Assemble the browser as a columns tree
set.outcome:
**The theme browser is the page.** [/imagine/design/themes/](/imagine/design/themes/) — a columns tree under /imagine/: a rail of themes, the wall open beside it at first paint, one column per theme, one for the generator, one for the proposal.

![](wall.jpg)

**Five alternates, token-only classes** — [press](/imagine/design/themes/press/) (editorial cream, serif, oxblood) · [phosphor](/imagine/design/themes/phosphor/) (CRT mono green, dark in *both* modes, declines the mode axis) · [bloom](/imagine/design/themes/bloom/) (high-key pastel, 1em radius) · [oled](/imagine/design/themes/oled/) (pure #000 / pure #fff, hairlines, no shadow either mode) · [riso](/imagine/design/themes/riso/) (fluoro pink over midnight blue on newsprint). Each is painted on the same mock mini-UI — nav strip, card, `button.prim` + quiet, code chip, link — with a live swatch strip, and each column lists every property it declares, **read back out of the stylesheet, not retyped**.

**[Generated](/imagine/design/themes/generated/) runs live** — `generate.js`, no dependencies: seed (hue, chroma, lightness curve, contrast floor) → OKLCH → sRGB → a 20-step bisection that *solves* each ink token's lightness against the surface it will sit on. Six seeds, ratios measured after the fact: ink 7.0–9.5:1, subtle and prim-ink on target. The point is the fourth figure — `--prim` measures **2.8–3.0:1 as text** on every light seed, the exact shape of the live defects the colour study found (`ext/AITask` 2.25:1, `ext/toc` 2.01:1). A generator cannot ship that, because fill and ink are two different solves.

![](generated.jpg)

**The seam holds; three things it does not carry.** (1) **Selectors don't stand down.** `lew42.css` styles buttons as `.theme-lew42 :is(button, .btn)`, so a *nested* theme keeps lew42's uppercase CTA voice whatever class it wears — invisible in production, and exactly why a nested preview can lie. (2) **`--card-shadow` is a colour inside a geometry the theme can't reach** (`Page.css:654`) — riso wanted a hard 5px offset and had to write a rule; the missing token is the shadow, not its colour. (3) **Lighting the code box costs ten more tokens** — the colour study's `--syn-*` trap, confirmed by building it. Every other token cascaded cleanly.

**[Proposal](/imagine/design/themes/proposal/) — 3 next steps.** 1. Promote `press` + `oled` into `styles/layers/theme/`, picker in the sidebar footer, `store_key: "theme"` on the root — ~3h. 2. Give the shadow a token (`--card-lift`, the whole `box-shadow`) — ~2h. 3. Fold the generator into `ext/`, four sliders and a Copy button — ~4h.

**Left deliberately:** no `readme.md` (the design record is `themes.css`'s header and the Proposal column); `themes-` and the five `theme-<name>` prefixes are **unregistered** in `styles/css-scopes.txt` — that file is inside the fence, one line each for whoever lands this. **First thing to cut:** `bloom` — least distinguishable tile on the wall, and the only theme carrying a second full syntax palette.
